question: What are the state-of-the-art work for 3D Mesh Generation from Multi-view 2d images?

sections.title: Background & Challenges
sections.text:
TLDR; Reconstructing 3D meshes from 2D images is fundamentally challenging due to missing depth information and ambiguity. Early approaches relied on traditional computer vision techniques, while modern deep learning methods aim to overcome limitations of computation and complexity. (5 sources)

Reconstructing 3D meshes from 2D images represents a fundamental challenge in computer vision and graphics because converting 2D projections into a complete 3D representation requires solving an inherently ambiguous problem - multiple valid 3D structures could correspond to the same 2D observation  [253499424 | Li et al. | 2022 | Citations: 20]. This challenge makes it particularly difficult to preserve both geometric accuracy and surface details in the final output.

Traditional approaches tackled this challenge using established computer vision pipelines that combined Structure from Motion (SfM), Multi-View Stereo (MVS), and mesh surface extraction techniques  [270123803 | Wu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 52] [19672940 | Schönberger et al. | 2016 | Citations: 3946]. These methods, while effective, were computationally intensive and often struggled to handle complex geometries or scale efficiently  [270123803 | Wu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 52].

Modern approaches have evolved to embrace deep learning solutions that offer potentially better efficiency <Model name="Anthropic" version="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022">. Notable developments have included the introduction of deep learning-based mesh completion systems that can operate entirely in 3D space  [52117356 | Huang et al. | 2018 | Citations: 400] and approaches that jointly learn geometry and texture processing  [44990860 | Yao et al. | 2018 | Citations: 575]. Despite these advances, current systems continue to face trade-offs between computational efficiency and reconstruction quality, particularly when dealing with complex geometric features or intricate textures  [270123803 | Wu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 52].

citations.title: [253499424 | Li et al. | 2022 | Citations: 20]
snippets: The goal of image-based mesh generation is to infer the 3D mesh of objects or scenes from one or multiple 2D images. Recovery of the lost dimensions from just 2D images is an ill-posed problem and fundamental to many applications, such as robot navigation, 3D modeling and animation, industrial control, and medical diagnosis. The rapid development of deep learning techniques, and more importantly, the increasing public datasets, accelerate the evolution of this subfield. Despite being recent, these methods have demonstrated exciting and promising results on various tasks (Han et al., 2019)...Sinha et al. (Sinha et al., 2017) constructed networks to learn geometric images with images as input to generate 3D meshes. The geometric information of the shape is preserved by parameterization learning. Wang et al. (Wang et al., 2018) used the deformation-based approach to restore geometry and topology. Afterward, there were many deformation-based methods (Wen et al., 2019), (Wang et al., 2020)- (Yang et al., 2020). Wen et al. (Wen et al., 2019) used multiple images to build geometric details, as shown in 14. Tong et al. [18] employed specific templates to provide more geometric details...Henderson et al. (Henderson et al., 2020) focused on the problem of generating a 3D texture mesh from 2D images. Munkberg et al. (Munkberg et al., 2021) simultaneously optimized topology, materials, and illumination from multiview image observations...mesh generation based on image sequences and videos is also worthy of attention (Yang et al., 2021), [28], (Pedone et al., 2020), (Jiang et al., 2022), (Bovzivc et al., 2021), (Sun et al., 2021).

citations.title: [270123803 | Wu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 52]
snippets: In this work, we introduce Unique3D, a novel image-to-3D framework for efficiently generating high-quality 3D meshes from single-view images, featuring state-of-the-art generation fidelity and strong generalizability. Previous methods based on Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) can produce diversified 3D results by distilling 3D knowledge from large 2D diffusion models, but they usually suffer from long per-case optimization time with inconsistent issues. Recent works address the problem and generate better 3D results either by finetuning a multi-view diffusion model or training a fast feed-forward model. However, they still lack intricate textures and complex geometries due to inconsistency and limited generated resolution. To simultaneously achieve high fidelity, consistency, and efficiency in single image-to-3D, we propose a novel framework Unique3D that includes a multi-view diffusion model with a corresponding normal diffusion model to generate multi-view images with their normal maps, a multi-level upscale process to progressively improve the resolution of generated orthographic multi-views, as well as an instant and consistent mesh reconstruction algorithm called ISOMER, which fully integrates the color and geometric priors into mesh results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our Unique3D significantly outperforms other image-to-3D baselines in terms of geometric and textural details.

sections.title: Main Approaches
sections.text:
TLDR; Current 3D mesh generation from multi-view images falls into three main approaches: Score Distillation Sampling (SDS), Two-Stage Diffusion-based Generation, and Direct 3D Representation Learning. Each approach offers different trade-offs between quality, speed, and resource usage. (11 sources)

The landscape of 3D mesh generation from multi-view images has emerged along several distinct technical paths:

The Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) approach has become a foundational method, where 3D representations are optimized by comparing their rendered projections against those generated by pre-trained 2D diffusion models  [258034816 | Poole et al. | 2022 | Citations: 631]  [260167800 | Shen et al. | 2023 | Citations: 81]. This method has proven particularly effective for generating detailed textured meshes directly from images  [258034816 | Poole et al. | 2022 | Citations: 631].

A second major paradigm uses a two-stage pipeline consisting of multi-view image generation followed by 3D reconstruction  [271534150 | Tang et al. | 2024 | Citations: 17]. This approach has gained traction through innovations in both stages, with notable implementations like DreamComposer showing how multi-view consistency can be achieved through feature matching and refinement processes  [259286991 | Liu et al. | 2023 | Citations: 441].

The third approach focuses on direct 3D representation learning, utilizing specialized architectures that bypass intermediate 2D generations entirely. This includes hybrid approaches combining VAEs with GANs for direct mesh generation  [257940142 | Ajayi et al. | 2023 | Citations: 1] and methods that integrate 3D-aware attention mechanisms for maintaining consistency across views  (Liu et al._1,  2023).

Each of these approaches faces unique challenges. SDS-based methods can be slow and memory-intensive, while two-stage approaches may inherit limitations from the underlying 2D generators. Direct 3D methods risk suffering from blurry artifacts in unseen regions  [274514958 | Hu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]. Recent work has begun exploring alternatives beyond these established paradigms, including the use of 3D variational auto-encoders and direct 3D diffusion models  [277321546 | Chen et al. | 2025 | Citations: 1]  [269983485 | Xie et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1].

The field continues to evolve rapidly, with newer methods increasingly focusing on balancing generation speed, output quality, and computational efficiency  [258523614 | Zhao et al. | 2023 | Citations: 91]. Cross-domain attention mechanisms and geometry-aware fusion algorithms have emerged as promising solutions for improving consistency across different views and modalities  [264436465 | Long et al. | 2023 | Citations: 405].

citations.title: [257940142 | Ajayi et al. | 2023 | Citations: 1]
snippets: This paper presents an approach that integrates a variational autoencoder (VAE) and a generative adversarial network (GAN) called 3 dimensional variational autoencoder signed distance function generative adversarial network (3D-VAE-SDFGAN) to create a 3D shape from a 2D image that considerably improves scalability and visual quality. The proposed method only feeds a single 2D image into the network to produce a mesh-based 3D shape. The network encodes a 2D image of the 3D object into the latent representations, and implicit surface representations of 3D objects corresponding to those 2D images are subsequently generated. Hence, a signed distance function (SDF) is proposed to maintain object inside-outside information in the implicit surface representation. Polygon mesh surfaces are then produced using the marching cubes algorithm.

citations.title: [259286991 | Liu et al. | 2023 | Citations: 441]
snippets: Single image 3D reconstruction is an important but challenging task that requires extensive knowledge of our natural world. Many existing methods solve this problem by optimizing a neural radiance field under the guidance of 2D diffusion models but suffer from lengthy optimization time, 3D inconsistency results, and poor geometry. In this work, we propose a novel method that takes a single image of any object as input and generates a full 360-degree 3D textured mesh in a single feed-forward pass. Given a single image, we first use a view-conditioned 2D diffusion model, Zero123, to generate multi-view images for the input view, and then aim to lift them up to 3D space. Since traditional reconstruction methods struggle with inconsistent multi-view predictions, we build our 3D reconstruction module upon an SDF-based generalizable neural surface reconstruction method and propose several critical training strategies to enable the reconstruction of 360-degree meshes. Without costly optimizations, our method reconstructs 3D shapes in significantly less time than existing methods. Moreover, our method favors better geometry, generates more 3D consistent results, and adheres more closely to the input image. We evaluate our approach on both synthetic data and in-the-wild images and demonstrate its superiority in terms of both mesh quality and runtime. In addition, our approach can seamlessly support the text-to-3D task by integrating with off-the-shelf text-to-image diffusion models.

citations.title: [260167800 | Shen et al. | 2023 | Citations: 81]
snippets: This work considers gradient-based mesh optimization, where we iteratively optimize for a 3D surface mesh by representing it as the isosurface of a scalar field, an increasingly common paradigm in applications including photogrammetry, generative modeling, and inverse physics. Existing implementations adapt classic isosurface extraction algorithms like Marching Cubes or Dual Contouring; these techniques were designed to extract meshes from fixed, known fields, and in the optimization setting they lack the degrees of freedom to represent high-quality feature-preserving meshes, or suffer from numerical instabilities. We introduce FlexiCubes, an isosurface representation specifically designed for optimizing an unknown mesh with respect to geometric, visual, or even physical objectives. Our main insight is to introduce additional carefully-chosen parameters into the representation, which allow local flexible adjustments to the extracted mesh geometry and connectivity. These parameters are updated along with the underlying scalar field via automatic differentiation when optimizing for a downstream task. We base our extraction scheme on Dual Marching Cubes for improved topological properties, and present extensions to optionally generate tetrahedral and hierarchically-adaptive meshes. Extensive experiments validate FlexiCubes on both synthetic benchmarks and real-world applications, showing that it offers significant improvements in mesh quality and geometric fidelity.

citations.title: [264436465 | Long et al. | 2023 | Citations: 405]
snippets: In this work, we introduce Wonder3D, a novel method for efficiently generating high-fidelity textured meshes from single-view images. Recent methods based on Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) have shown the potential to recover 3D geometry from 2D diffusion priors, but they typically suffer from time-consuming per-shape optimization and inconsistent geometry. In contrast, certain works di-rectly produce 3D information via fast network inferences, but their results are often of low quality and lack geometric details. To holistically improve the quality, consistency, and efficiency of single-view reconstruction tasks, we pro-pose a cross-domain diffusion model that generates multi-view normal maps and the corresponding color images. To ensure the consistency of generation, we employ a multi-view cross-domain attention mechanism that facilitates information exchange across views and modalities. Lastly, we introduce a geometry-aware normal fusion algorithm that extracts high-quality surfaces from the multi-view 2D representations in only 2 r-;» 3 minutes. Our extensive evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves high-quality reconstruction results, robust generalization, and good efficiency compared to prior works.

citations.title: [269983485 | Xie et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]
snippets:
Previous efforts have managed to generate production-ready 3D assets from text or images. However, these methods primarily employ NeRF or 3D Gaussian representations, which are not adept at producing smooth, high-quality geometries required by modern rendering pipelines.

Zero123 [18] demonstrates that large diffusion models have learned rich 3D priors about the visual world, even though they are only trained on 2D images. Furthermore, they introduce the first refined diffusion model capable of generating plausible images of objects from any viewpoint. A series of subsequent works [30,31,19,20] have focused on enhancing the 3D consistency and resolution of multiview images generated by diffusion models. Zero123++ [30] proposes that generating consistent multi-view images hinges on accurately modeling their joint distribution and integrates six images in a 3×2 layout into a single frame for simultaneous multi-view generation during one diffusion process. MVDream [31] and Wonder3D [20] both recommend implementing multi-view attentions to enable feature sharing during the multi-view generation process. Free3D [43] introduces Plücker Embeddings of pixels in images' corresponding rays and a Ray Conditional Normalization layer during the diffusion generation process, which helps to produce multi-view images with more accurate perspectives. Although these methods have generated impressive multi-view images, achieving 3D consistency among them remains a challenge.

Recent breakthroughs in multi-view diffusion model [27] have rapidly sparked interest [25,18] in reconstructing 3D content generation from various conditions, such as Text and images, known as 2D-lifting, include distillation-based approaches and reconstructed-based approaches. Distillation-based approaches, exemplified by Dreamfusion and Magic3D [25,14], leverage 2D diffusion models for optimizing 3D representations through score distillation sampling (SDS). The reconstructed-based approaches are notably represented by Zero123 and SyncDreamer [18,19], which involves generating images with multi-view consistency using diffusion models, followed by employing volume rendering techniques to optimize 3D representations, such as neural radiance fields (NeRF) [22]or signed distance functions (SDF) [34].

snippets: Recent 3D large reconstruction models typically employ a two-stage process, including first generate multi-view images by a multi-view diffusion model, and then utilize a feed-forward model to reconstruct images to 3D content.

Instant3D [16] offers a fast method for creating high-quality 3D assets from text prompts by combining sparse-view generation with a transformer-based reconstructor [8,52,55,(Zhang et al., 2024), significantly reducing inference time. MVDream [40] employs a multi-view diffusion model to improve consistency and stability in 3D generation, integrating 2D and 3D data. SyncDreamer [23] enhances multiview-consistency from a single-view image using a 3D-aware feature attention mechanism. citations.title: [277321546 | Chen et al. | 2025 | Citations: 1]
snippets: Recent advances in open-world 3D object generation have demonstrated promising results following several distinct paradigms. Large Reconstruction Models [13,39] employ transformers to convert single images into 3D shapes through implicit representations with multi-view supervision. However, the lack of generative priors leads to blurry artifacts in unseen regions. Another direction combines 2D diffusion models [4,21,23,33,41] with sparse view 3D reconstruction models [18,37,46,48]. However, these methods are constrained by the quality and consistency of the generated multi-view images. A more recent paradigm follows the success of 2D image generation by utilizing 3D variational auto-encoders (VAE) to compress dense point clouds into latent space, then applying diffusion models for direct 3D shape generation (Hu et al., 2024)20,[50][51](Zhao et al., 2023).

sections.title: State-of-the-Art Methods
sections.text:
TLDR; Recent breakthrough methods focus on combining multi-view diffusion models with efficient 3D reconstruction pipelines. Key innovations include direct mesh generation from single images, improved geometric detail preservation, and enhanced view consistency through advanced attention mechanisms. (10 sources)

Here are the most notable recent methods in 3D mesh generation from multi-view images:

* **InstantMesh**: A feed-forward framework that generates high-quality 3D meshes in seconds by combining multi-view diffusion for consistent view synthesis with a specialized reconstruction model. Integrates differentiable isosurface extraction for direct mesh supervision, offering superior training scalability  [269033473 | Xu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 183].

* **Multi-view Large Reconstruction Model (M-LRM)**: Addresses limitations of single-image approaches by introducing multi-view consistent cross-attention schemes and 3D-aware token initialization. Achieves improved geometric and texture quality while maintaining computational efficiency  [270391527 | Li et al. | 2024 | Citations: 3].

* **Hi3D**: Leverages pre-trained video diffusion models to generate high-resolution multi-view images, enabling finer detail capture in 3D reconstructions. Focuses specifically on resolving the limitation of low-resolution multi-view inputs in previous approaches  [272593003 | Yang et al. | 2024 | Citations: 8].

* **SplatFace**: Introduces a Gaussian splatting framework specifically designed for human face reconstruction that doesn't require predetermined geometry. Simultaneously delivers high-quality novel view rendering and accurate 3D mesh reconstructions  [268724006 | Luo et al. | 2024 | Citations: 4].

* **Neural Mesh Fusion (NMF)**: Offers efficient joint optimization of polygon meshes from multi-view observations while performing unsupervised 3D planar-segmentation. Significantly more computationally efficient than implicit neural rendering approaches  [268032560 | Zanjani et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1].

* **Unique3D**: Combines multi-view diffusion with direct mesh unprojection to achieve sharp surface details. While slightly slower than feed-forward approaches, excels in geometry reconstruction quality  [274233867 | Yu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]  [270123803 | Wu et al. | 2025 | Citations: 52].

* **SV3D**: Utilizes a latent video diffusion model for multi-view synthesis with explicit camera control capabilities. Incorporates spatial-temporal attention to improve 3D reconstruction quality  [274514958 | Hu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]  [270370869 | Zhuang et al. | 2024 | Citations: 6].

* **One-2-3**: Demonstrates efficient single-image 3D reconstruction without extensive optimization, achieving real-time performance while maintaining consistent mesh generation  [274514958 | Hu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1].

citations.title: [268032560 | Zanjani et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]
snippets: Neural Mesh Fusion (NMF), an efficient approach for joint optimization of polygon mesh from multi-view image observations and unsupervised 3D planar-surface parsing of the scene. In contrast to implicit neural representations, NMF directly learns to deform surface triangle mesh and generate an embedding for unsupervised 3D planar segmentation through gradient-based optimization directly on the surface mesh. The conducted experiments show that NMF obtains competitive results compared to state-of-the-art multi-view planar reconstruction, while not requiring any ground-truth 3D or planar supervision. Moreover, NMF is significantly more computationally efficient compared to implicit neural rendering-based scene reconstruction approaches.

snippets: We present SplatFace, a novel Gaussian splatting framework designed for 3D human face reconstruction without reliance on accurate pre-determined geometry. Our method is designed to simultaneously deliver both high-quality novel view rendering and accurate 3D mesh reconstructions.

citations.title: [269033473 | Xu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 183]
snippets: In this work, we present InstantMesh, a feed-forward framework for high-quality 3D mesh generation from a single image. Given an input image, InstantMesh first generates 3D consistent multi-view images with a multi-view diffusion model, and then utilizes a sparse-view large reconstruction model to predict a 3D mesh directly, where the whole process can be accomplished in seconds. By integrating a differentiable iso-surface extraction module, our reconstruction model applies geometric supervisions on the mesh surface directly, enabling satisfying training efficiency and mesh generation quality. Building upon an LRM-based architecture, our model offers superior training scalability to large-scale datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that InstantMesh outperforms other latest image-to-3D approaches significantly.

citations.title: [270370869 | Zhuang et al. | 2024 | Citations: 6]
snippets: We propose a novel approach for 3D mesh reconstruction from multi-view images. Our method takes inspiration from large reconstruction models like LRM [11] that use a transformer-based triplane generator and a Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) model trained on multi-view images. However, in our method, we introduce several important modifications that allow us to significantly enhance 3D reconstruction quality. First of all, we examine the original LRM architecture and find several shortcomings. Subsequently, we introduce respective modifications to the LRM architecture, which lead to improved multi-view image representation and more computationally efficient training. Second, in order to improve geometry reconstruction and enable supervision at full image resolution, we extract meshes from the NeRF field in a differentiable manner and fine-tune the NeRF model through mesh rendering. These modifications allow us to achieve state-of-the-art performance on both 2D and 3D evaluation metrics, such as a PSNR of 28.67 on Google Scanned Objects (GSO) dataset.

citations.title: [270391527 | Li et al. | 2024 | Citations: 3]
snippets: Despite recent advancements in the Large Reconstruction Model (LRM) demonstrating impressive results, when extending its input from single image to multiple images, it exhibits inefficiencies, subpar geometric and texture quality, as well as slower convergence speed than expected. It is attributed to that, LRM formulates 3D reconstruction as a naive images-to-3D translation problem, ignoring the strong 3D coherence among the input images. In this paper, we propose a Multi-view Large Reconstruction Model (M-LRM) designed to reconstruct high-quality 3D shapes from multi-views in a 3D-aware manner. Specifically, we introduce a multi-view consistent cross-attention scheme to enable M-LRM to accurately query information from the input images. Moreover, we employ the 3D priors of the input multi-view images to initialize the triplane tokens.

citations.title: [272593003 | Yang et al. | 2024 | Citations: 8]
snippets: Despite having tremendous progress in image-to-3D generation, existing methods still struggle to produce multi-view consistent images with high-resolution textures in detail, especially in the paradigm of 2D diffusion that lacks 3D awareness. In this work, we present High-resolution Image-to-3D model (Hi3D), a new video diffusion based paradigm that redefines a single image to multi-view images as 3D-aware sequential image generation (i.e., orbital video generation). This methodology delves into the underlying temporal consistency knowledge in video diffusion model that generalizes well to geometry consistency across multiple views in 3D generation. Technically, Hi3D first empowers the pre-trained video diffusion model with 3D-aware prior (camera pose condition), yielding multi-view images with low-resolution texture details. A 3D-aware video-to-video refiner is learnt to further scale up the multi-view images with high-resolution texture details. Such high-resolution multi-view images are further augmented with novel views through 3D Gaussian Splatting, which are finally leveraged to obtain high-fidelity meshes via 3D reconstruction. Extensive experiments on both novel view synthesis and single view reconstruction demonstrate that our Hi3D manages to produce superior multi-view consistency images with highly-detailed textures. Source code and data are available at https://github.com/yanghb22-fdu/Hi3D-Official.

citations.title: [274233867 | Yu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]
snippets: Benefiting from diffusion models [11] and large-scale 3D datasets [6], the task of reconstructing colored 3D mesh from a single image has made significant progress. The pioneer work DreamFusion [29] utilizes 2D diffusion models for 3D generation via score distillation sampling. To improve novel-view plausibility, multiview [32]40] or view-conditioned (Liu et al., 2023) diffusion models are developed. With their generated multiview images as reference, 3D meshes can be generated via NeuS (Liu et al., 2023)(Wang et al., 2021), normal fusion (Long et al., 2023), etc. To improve speed, researchers propose LRM (Hong et al., 2023), which is a feed-forward network trained with extensive 3D data for 3D generation, given single image or diffusion-generated multiview images as input. Besides, 3D diffusion models (Lan et al., 2024) or video diffusion models (Yang et al., 2024) are also used for 3D generation, yet not as popular as diffusion and LRM so far. While most exist-  ing methods yield blurry-looking meshes, Unique3D (Wu et al., 2024) achieves a clear appearance by unprojecting multiview images to the mesh, although its geometry reconstruction is slower and often yields artifacts compared to LRM.

sections.title: Technical Innovations
sections.text:
TLDR; Recent technical innovations focus on addressing key challenges through novel architectural designs and optimization strategies. Major advances include 3D-aware attention mechanisms, direct mesh manipulation frameworks, and improved handling of sparse view inputs. (11 sources)

The latest technical innovations in 3D mesh generation from multi-view images center around several groundbreaking approaches. A significant advancement comes from the development of cost-volume based neural surface reconstruction methods that can handle inconsistent multi-view predictions while operating without requiring precise camera poses  (Liu et al._2,  2023)  [252895043 | Long et al. | 2022 | Citations: 274].

Direct mesh manipulation has emerged as a crucial innovation path, with Neural Mesh Fusion (NMF) leading the way by enabling joint optimization of polygon meshes while simultaneously performing unsupervised 3D planar segmentation, offering substantial computational advantages over implicit neural approaches  [268032560 | Zanjani et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1].

Another key innovation addresses the challenge of limited input views through the integration of geometric priors and generalizable constraints. New methods can now reconstruct high-quality meshes from sparse views by leveraging neural implicit representations and differentiable rendering  [272524504 | Ye et al. | 2024 | Citations: 3]  [233649017 | Wang et al. | 2021 | Citations: 513].

Cross-domain attention mechanisms have proven particularly effective for improving view consistency and geometric accuracy. These innovations facilitate better information exchange between different views and modalities, leading to more coherent 3D reconstructions  (Wang et al._1,  2024)  [264436465 | Long et al. | 2023 | Citations: 405].

Recent advances in graph-based approaches have introduced iterative vertex deformation strategies that learn to exploit cross-view information effectively. These methods achieve superior performance by searching for optimal vertex positions in local neighborhoods  [248299984 | Wen et al. | 2022 | Citations: 16]  [102350340 | Wen et al. | 2019 | Citations: 287].

Material and illumination optimization has seen notable improvements through unified optimization frameworks that simultaneously handle topology, materials, and illumination from multi-view observations  [253499424 | Li et al. | 2022 | Citations: 20]  [235659762 | Munkberg et al. | 2021 | Citations: 171].

citations.title: [248299984 | Wen et al. | 2022 | Citations: 16]
snippets: We propose a graph convolutional framework to produce 3D mesh model from multiple images. Our model learns to exploit cross-view information and generates vertex deformation iteratively to improve the mesh produced from the direct prediction methods, e.g. Pixel2Mesh and its multi-view extension. Inspired by multi-view geometry methods, our model searches in the nearby area around each vertex for an optimal place to relocate it. Compared to previous works, our model achieves the state-ofthe-art performance, produces shapes containing accurate surface details rather than merely visually plausible from input views, and shows good generalization capability in many aspects.

The rapid development of deep learning techniques, and more importantly, the increasing public datasets, accelerate the evolution of this subfield. In contrast to implicit neural representations, NMF directly learns to deform surface triangle mesh and generate an embedding for unsupervised 3D planar segmentation through gradient-based optimization directly on the surface mesh. citations.title: [272524504 | Ye et al. | 2024 | Citations: 3]
snippets: Neural implicit representations have revolutionized dense multi-view surface reconstruction, yet their performance significantly diminishes with sparse input views. A few pioneering works have sought to tackle this challenge by leveraging additional geometric priors or multi-scene generalizability. However, they are still hindered by the imperfect choice of input views, using images under empirically determined viewpoints...Recently, neural implicit methods (Wang et al., 2021)(Yariv et al., 2021) propose to represent the scene as a signed distance field (SDF) and optimize mesh surfaces directly from 2D image supervision through differentiable rendering. Although neural implicit methods surpass previous works in achieving high-fidelity mesh reconstruction, they typically rely on densely captured images as inputs, whose acquisition process can be time-consuming. To alleviate this reliance, some methods attempt to reconstruct 3D mesh from a predefined set of sparse views, based on geometric priors (Yu et al., 2022) or generalizable priors (Long et al., 2022).

sections.title: Performance & Limitations
sections.text:
TLDR; Current methods face trade-offs between generation speed, output quality, and computational resources. Key limitations include poor feature disentangling in latent spaces, difficulties with complex geometries, and challenges in maintaining consistency across views. (5 sources)

Recent evaluations reveal significant trade-offs in current 3D mesh generation approaches. While newer methods have achieved impressive generation speeds, they often sacrifice fidelity to input images  (Liu et al._2,  2023). For instance, approaches like Zero123 can produce textured 3D meshes in under 45 seconds, but the primary challenge remains ensuring 3D consistency across generated views  (Liu et al._2,  2023).

A fundamental limitation lies in the entanglement of various visual attributes within conventional latent spaces, where factors like lighting, material properties, and structural elements become mixed, making it difficult to achieve realistic predictions even when additional views are incorporated  [272599742 | Chen et al. | 2024 | Citations: 0]. This challenge persists despite attempts to improve controllability through multi-view integration.

Input constraints continue to limit performance potential. Most current approaches are restricted by a relatively small and fixed number of input views, which can result in incomplete or suboptimal reconstructions, especially when the synthesized views are of lower quality  [273022678 | Han et al. | 2024 | Citations: 4]. The problem becomes particularly acute when working with complex geometries or intricate surface details.

While recent architectures like Large Reconstruction Models (LRMs) have shown promise, they still struggle with maintaining high geometric and texture quality while scaling to multi-view inputs. These models often exhibit slower convergence rates and reduced efficiency compared to their single-view counterparts  [270391527 | Li et al. | 2024 | Citations: 3]. The challenge stems from treating 3D reconstruction as a straightforward image-to-3D translation problem, failing to adequately account for the natural 3D coherence that exists among multiple views.

snippets: Recently, methods like Zero-1-2-3 have focused on single-view based 3D reconstruction and have achieved remarkable success. However, their predictions for unseen areas heavily rely on the inductive bias of large-scale pretrained diffusion models. Although subsequent work, such as DreamComposer, attempts to make predictions more controllable by incorporating additional views, the results remain unrealistic due to feature entanglement in the vanilla latent space, including factors such as lighting, material, and structure.

citations.title: [273022678 | Han et al. | 2024 | Citations: 4]
snippets: Generating high-quality 3D content from text, single images, or sparse view images remains a challenging task with broad applications. Existing methods typically employ multi-view diffusion models to synthesize multi-view images, followed by a feed-forward process for 3D reconstruction. However, these approaches are often constrained by a small and fixed number of input views, limiting their ability to capture diverse viewpoints and, even worse, leading to suboptimal generation results if the synthesized views are of poor quality.

question: What 2d barcode is resilient to compression?

sections.title: Introduction to 2D Barcodes
sections.text:
TLDR; Two-dimensional barcodes evolved from traditional linear barcodes to offer enhanced data storage and resilience. They represent binary data in a grid-based format that leverages both horizontal and vertical spaces for encoding information. (3 sources)

Two-dimensional barcodes marked a significant advancement over their linear predecessors by introducing capabilities for both data location and error tolerance  [256241331 | Wu | 2017 | Citations: 1]. Their evolution represents a fundamental shift from simple linear patterns to sophisticated grid-based systems that utilize both horizontal and vertical dimensions for data encoding. This innovation was driven by the need for more robust and higher-capacity data storage solutions. The development of modern 2D barcodes drew inspiration from earlier work like Code 49, but took a crucial step forward by utilizing both axes simultaneously to fill two-dimensional space with specialized square blocks, each serving specific encoding purposes  [259422131 | Seta | 2023 | Citations: 13]. While traditional 2D barcodes focus primarily on storing and retrieving information, newer variations have expanded their capabilities to include additional functionalities such as tracking and authentication features <Model name="Anthropic" version="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022">.

citations.title: [256241331 | Wu | 2017 | Citations: 1]
snippets: Compared with older linear barcodes, 2D barcodes are a machine-readable representation of binary data that possess capabilities of location and tolerance.

citations.title: [259422131 | Seta | 2023 | Citations: 13]
snippets: In his search for a symbology that could encode more data, was faster to read and more resilient to damage than linear barcodes, Hara found inspiration in David Allais' Code 49 and improved it with a key intuition: rather than stacking horizontal rows of bars, his prototype utilized both vertical and horizontal axes (Goodrich, 2020), filling a two-dimensional space with square block modules dedicated to specific encoding functions.

sections.title: Resilient 2D Barcode Types
sections.text:
TLDR; Several advanced 2D barcode variants have been developed specifically to withstand compression and environmental challenges. These include color-based systems, blur-resistant designs, and vector quantization-compatible codes that maintain readability despite image manipulation. (4 sources)

* **QR Codes**: Feature built-in error correction mechanisms that allow partial damage without compromising data integrity. They can be divided into multiple data areas, enabling reconstruction of complete information even if parts of the code are damaged  [13436529 | Liu et al. | 2012 | Citations: 42]

* **BGW Barcoding System**: Offers unique compression capabilities that allow encoding more information while maintaining the same physical dimensions of the barcode symbol. Can achieve compression rates of 17-25%, depending on configuration parameters  [198338076 | Onai et al. | 2019 | Citations: 1]

* **Blur-Robust (BR) Code**: Specifically engineered to resist defocus blur through the use of blur-invariant concentric ring finder patterns and geometric features. Demonstrates 21% better resistance to blur compared to QR codes, maintaining readability even in severely blurred conditions  [233472630 | Xie et al. | 2021 | Citations: 2]

* **Vector Quantization (VQ)-Compatible QR Codes**: Designed to preserve embedded VQ-compressed codes even when the QR code shows visible distortions, ensuring data recoverability despite image manipulations  [30210052 | Wu | 2017 | Citations: 13]

* **Color-Based High-Density Systems**: Advanced symbologies that leverage color coding to maximize data density while maintaining resilience against common imaging impairments typical in smartphone photography  (Wu_1,  2017)

snippets: Based on their superior characteristics [18]. It can be divided into multiple data areas, and information stored in multiple QR code symbols can be reconstructed as a single data symbol, allowing high error tolerance. sections.title: Error Correction and Tolerance Mechanisms
sections.text:
TLDR; Modern 2D barcodes employ sophisticated error correction mechanisms including fault-tolerant division of data areas and redundancy checking units. These features allow the codes to maintain functionality even when partially damaged or corrupted. (3 sources)

Advanced 2D barcodes incorporate multiple layers of protection to ensure reliable data retrieval even under adverse conditions. At the core of their resilience is the concept of fault tolerance, where QR codes are deliberately designed with error correction capabilities that can compensate for damaged areas as long as they remain within specified limits  (Chen et al._1,  2020). To optimize this fault tolerance feature, developers have implemented innovative approaches such as artificially dividing the 2D barcode into distinct zones, some of which can contain alternative information while preserving the primary data access capability  (Chen et al._1,  2020).

Another notable approach to enhancing durability involves the integration of redundancy checking units within the encoding sequence. By inserting XOR operation results between sets of three adjacent encoded units, these systems can significantly boost their interference resistance, though this comes with a trade-off of approximately 25% reduction in storage capacity  [226559394 | Jin et al. | 2020 | Citations: 1]. Research continues to advance in this field, with particular attention being paid to improving noise immunity to ensure consistently error-free scanning experiences  [219434572 | Dychka et al. | 2020 | Citations: 1].

These error correction mechanisms collectively create a robust framework that maintains data accessibility even when portions of the barcode are obscured or damaged <Model name="Anthropic" version="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022">.

sections.title: Compression Impact and Solutions
sections.text:
TLDR; Image compression poses significant challenges for 2D barcode readability due to artifacts and loss of detail. However, solutions exist ranging from strategic compression parameter selection to proactive data compression before encoding. (3 sources)

Compression-related issues present a complex challenge for 2D barcode implementation, particularly affecting their localization and accurate reading. When dealing with video compression, for instance, studies have shown that barcode readability remains relatively stable across a wide range of compression settings, specifically when using quantization parameters (QP) from 10 to 42, although excessive downsampling does increase the risk of missed detections  [246852553 | Hendrikx et al. | 2022 | Citations: 0].

To address these limitations, several effective strategies have emerged. One practical approach involves proactively compressing the data before encoding it into 2D barcodes, particularly for image-based data which typically consumes more space. This preprocessing step can effectively expand the overall data capacity of the resulting barcode  [6860055 | Lyons et al. | 2010 | Citations: 17]  [65033803 | Kumar et al. | 2017 | Citations: 2]. More sophisticated methods have been developed that integrate Vector Quantization (VQ) compressed codes directly into QR codes, demonstrating that meaningful data can be recovered even when the QR code exhibits noticeable visual distortions  [30210052 | Wu | 2017 | Citations: 13].

These solutions demonstrate that while compression challenges exist, careful implementation strategies can maintain barcode functionality while managing file sizes <Model name="Anthropic" version="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022">.

sections.title: Background & Motivation
sections.text:
TLDR; Traditional information retrieval systems have been transformed by transformer-based models, particularly in ranking tasks. While these models show impressive capabilities, they face challenges related to computational costs and the need for more interpretable designs. (5 sources)

Recent developments in information retrieval (IR) have been marked by a significant shift towards transformer-based approaches, especially in addressing fundamental challenges in the field. One of the primary challenges in IR has been bridging the gap between lexical matching and semantic understanding, as well as moving beyond the traditional probabilistic frameworks  [202540869 | Yan et al. | 2019 | Citations: 328]. Large pretrained language models, particularly those based on transformers, have emerged as powerful tools for enhancing retrieval performance, with their effectiveness largely dependent on both architectural choices and the semantic complexity of input text  [263297581 | Pan et al. | 2023 | Citations: 5].

However, despite their demonstrated success, transformer-based ranking models face notable challenges. These include high computational demands and difficulties in interpreting the ranking process due to their opaque hidden states  [216562742 | Gao et al. | 2020 | Citations: 9]. This tension between performance and practicality has spurred innovation in model design, leading to various approaches such as ensemble methods that combine multiple specialized models using techniques like LambdaMART or XGBoost to produce final relevance scores  [227230573 | Zhang et al. | 2020 | Citations: 4]  [8833939 | Chen et al. | 2016 | Citations: 10841]. These developments highlight the ongoing pursuit of balancing sophisticated model capabilities with operational efficiency and interpretability <Model name="Anthropic" version="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022">.

citations.title: [216562742 | Gao et al. | 2020 | Citations: 9]
snippets: This paper presents a novel Embed Ahead Rank Later (EARL) framework, which speeds-up Transformer-based rankers by pre-computing representations and keeping online computation shallow. EARL dis-entangles the attention in a typical Transformer-based ranker into three asynchronous tasks and assign each to a dedicated Transformer: query understanding, document understanding, and relevance judging. With such a ranking framework, query and document token representations can be offline computed and reused.

citations.title: [227230573 | Zhang et al. | 2020 | Citations: 4]
snippets: Recent years have witnessed substantial progress in the development of neural ranking networks, but also an increasingly heavy computational burden due to growing numbers of parameters and the adoption of model ensembles.... Recently, BERT (Devlin et al., 2018), the pre-trained deep bidirectional Transformer, has shown strong performance on a broad range of language processing tasks and has wide application in ranking tasks as well (MacAvaney et al., 2019)Qiao et al., 2019). To further boost the results, it is common to adopt model ensembles, as modern neural ranking models provide a wealth of options for sub-models. The scores of all such sub-models with regard to the relevance of a candidate document to a query are collected and fed into a LambdaMART (Burges, 2010) or XGBoost (Chen et al., 2016) model to obtain the final ensemble relevance score.

citations.title: [263297581 | Pan et al. | 2023 | Citations: 5]
snippets: Recently, large pretrained language models (PLMs) have led a revolution in the information retrieval community. In most PLMs‐based retrieval frameworks, the ranking performance broadly depends on the model structure and the semantic complexity of the input text.

sections.title: Transformer Architectures in Ranking
sections.text:
TLDR; Two main types of transformer architectures dominate ranking applications: bi-encoders for efficient initial retrieval and cross-encoders for precise pairwise ranking. These architectures serve complementary roles, with bi-encoders handling large-scale retrieval and cross-encoders focusing on accurate top result refinement. (6 sources)

Transformer architectures have fundamentally changed how we approach ranking problems in information retrieval, offering significant improvements over conventional models  [266977631 | Vuong et al. | 2024 | Citations: 4]  [249365432 | Mustar et al. | 2021 | Citations: 5]. The field has evolved to recognize two distinct architectural approaches that serve different purposes in the ranking pipeline.

Bi-encoder architectures represent a practical solution for large-scale retrieval operations. These models process queries and documents separately, enabling efficient pre-computation and storage of document representations. This separation allows for quick retrieval responses by only computing the query representation during search time  [271571387 | Gienapp et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]. Due to their scalability and lower computational requirements, bi-encoders are typically employed for initial retrieval stages.

Cross-encoder architectures, on the other hand, focus on precise pairwise ranking by jointly computing document-query relevance scores. While these models achieve higher accuracy, they require significantly more computational resources and are primarily used in second-stage reranking processes, where they refine the top results identified by bi-encoders  [271571387 | Gienapp et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]. Notable implementations have demonstrated superior performance in capturing complex interactions between queries and documents  [72077346 | Nogueira et al. | 2019 | Citations: 860].

The implementation of transformer-based models in production environments comes with its own complexities, requiring careful consideration of engineering trade-offs and substantial technical expertise  [273877453 | Schlatt et al. | 2024 | Citations: 2]. To address these challenges, researchers have developed innovative approaches such as hierarchical transformer architectures, which employ multiple levels of encoding - from token-level to query-level representations - to better handle the nuances of different retrieval scenarios  [266977631 | Vuong et al. | 2024 | Citations: 4].

These architectural advances have consistently shown dramatic improvements in ranking performance across benchmark datasets  [253080555 | Bruch et al. | 2022 | Citations: 24], establishing transformer-based approaches as a cornerstone of modern information retrieval systems.

citations.title: [271571387 | Gienapp et al. | 2024 | Citations: 1]
snippets: In information retrieval, transformer-based bi-encoders are used as effective retrieval models. They estimate a document's relevance to a query by computing the similarity of their embeddings. Queries and documents are represented independently, which allows for pre-computing and indexing all document representations offline and computing only the query representation at retrieval time. biencoders are thus appealing in practice since they can be easily scaled. In contrast, transformer-based cross-encoders are a type of model that estimates relevance jointly by computing a score for each document-query pair at retrieval time, achieving higher effectiveness than bi-encoders at the expense of a higher computational cost and inference latency. They are thus usally reserved for multistage reranking, such that only the top-k documents of an initial ranking produced by a more efficient bi-encoder are re-ranked.

snippets: A wide range of transformer-based language models have been proposed for information retrieval tasks. However, including transformer-based models in retrieval pipelines is often complex and requires substantial engineering effort.

sections.title: Computational Challenges & Solutions
sections.text:
TLDR; Transformer-based ranking faces significant computational hurdles, particularly around speed and resource efficiency. Researchers have developed various solutions including precomputation strategies, modular designs, and selective architecture choices to balance performance with practical constraints. (8 sources)

While transformer-based models have proven highly effective for ranking tasks, their deployment in production environments faces substantial computational challenges  [248376951 | Mallia et al. | 2022 | Citations: 31]. The primary concerns center around processing speed and resource utilization, which have driven innovation in optimization strategies.

One major breakthrough came through the introduction of precomputation approaches. Models like Embed Ahead Rank Later (EARL) divide the ranking process into independent components for query understanding, document comprehension, and relevance assessment, allowing for offline computation of certain elements  (Gao et al._1,  2020). Similarly, the Transformer-Kernel (TK) model achieved competitive performance while reducing computational overhead through a minimalist approach with just two transformer layers and independent query-document encoding [233296348 | Mitra et al. | 2021 | Citations: 8].

Architectural innovations have played a crucial role in addressing these challenges. Late-interaction models, such as ColBERT, offer a middle ground between traditional keyword matching and comprehensive neural matching  [248376951 | Mallia et al. | 2022 | Citations: 31]  [219845435 | Khattab et al. | 2020 | Citations: 510]. Various late-interaction architectures, including Colbert and poly-encoder variants, have been developed to optimize throughput while maintaining ranking quality  [244463237 | Podberezko et al. | 2021 | Citations: 0].

Practical considerations have also led to hybrid approaches that combine different techniques. For instance, many systems now implement a two-step process where BM25 handles initial retrieval, followed by BERT-based re-ranking of top results [218581086 | Qadrud-Din et al. | 2020 | Citations: 5]. Recent research has expanded on this foundation with innovations like modular designs and query-directed sparse attention mechanisms  [256105432 | Hambarde et al. | 2023 | Citations: 56]. These approaches aim to maintain the benefits of transformer-based models while managing computational constraints effectively.

Specialized hardware solutions, such as Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), have also emerged as potential accelerators for transformer-based ranking  [248376951 | Mallia et al. | 2022 | Citations: 31]  [12893809 | Jouppi et al. | 2017 | Citations: 3371]. However, software optimizations remain central to making these models practical, with techniques ranging from approximate nearest neighbors to dynamic computation selection showing promise in improving real-world deployments  [248376951 | Mallia et al. | 2022 | Citations: 31]  [8221914 | Johnson et al. | 2017 | Citations: 901].

snippets: Most existing CNIR solutions proceed by first using a bag-of-words model such as BM25 to retrieve the initial set of relevant documents, and then using a BERT-based model to re-rank the top results (Dai et al., 2019), [13], [17], [23]. This two-step approach has been adopted because the recent transformer-based models are large, and using such a model to directly compare the query with each sentence in a corpus would be too computationally expensive, even if the corpus were relatively small. In our work, we explore the relative effectiveness of several different customized transformer-based models designed to work with vector nearest neighbor search indices.

Several of these approaches-e.g., (Yan et al., 2019)(Yilmaz et al., 2021)-employ BERT [17], with largescale pretraining, as their core architecture. Diverging from this trend, Hofstätter et al. Consequently, TK achieves competitive performance at a fraction of the training and inference cost of its BERT-based peers.

At the same time, they also pose new challenges, as transformers are very computationally expensive. This has motivated a lot of recent work on making transformer-based ranking more efficient. sections.title: Hierarchical & Multi-stage Approaches
sections.text:
TLDR; Modern information retrieval systems commonly employ multi-stage architectures that combine different transformer-based models and traditional approaches. These hybrid systems typically start with efficient initial retrieval followed by specialized reranking models, creating a balanced approach to precision and computational efficiency. (7 sources)

The evolution of information retrieval systems has embraced a layered approach that leverages both traditional and transformer-based methods in sequence  [231979055 | Lin et al. | 2021 | Citations: 80]. This multi-stage architecture has proven particularly effective, with systems typically beginning with either sparse retrieval methods like BM25 or dense retrieval using transformer-encoded representations, followed by more refined processing steps.

Ensemble approaches have emerged as a powerful strategy within these multi-stage architectures. Systems can combine multiple models through various strategies, including direct score averaging, rank fusion approaches, or supervised learning-to-rank techniques as meta-strategies  [231662318 | Borges et al. | 2021 | Citations: 0]. These ensemble methods allow systems to capitalize on the strengths of different architectural approaches while mitigating their respective weaknesses.

Recent innovations have focused on optimizing the integration of transformer-based rerankers within multi-stage pipelines. Lightweight reranking transformers (RRTs) have been developed to efficiently incorporate both local and global features in a single forward pass, effectively replacing more computationally intensive verification processes  [232320664 | Tan et al. | 2021 | Citations: 89]. This represents a significant advance in balancing accuracy with computational efficiency.

The effectiveness of these hierarchical approaches extends to specialized domains as well. For instance, in computer vision applications, multi-stage architectures combine visual-linguistic features through transformer-based combiners, demonstrating how these principles can be adapted across different modalities  [276776324 | Zhang et al. | 2025 | Citations: 0]. Similar hierarchical structures have been successful in query prediction tasks, where systems employ multiple levels of encoding to handle both token-level and query-level contextual representations  [266977631 | Vuong et al. | 2024 | Citations: 4].

An important advancement has been the recognition that different retrieval scenarios benefit from different types of transformer architectures  [240148987 | Zhang et al. | 2021 | Citations: 14]  [72077346 | Nogueira et al. | 2019 | Citations: 860]. This understanding has led to adaptive systems that can select appropriate architectures based on specific use cases, ensuring optimal performance across diverse retrieval scenarios.

sections.title: Current Research Directions
sections.text:
TLDR; Current research in transformer-based ranking focuses heavily on addressing information bottleneck challenges and improving the incorporation of feedback mechanisms. Key areas include developing more sophisticated graph-based architectures, exploring hierarchical attention patterns, and advancing multi-granularity supervision approaches. (7 sources)

Here are the current active research directions in transformer-based ranking:

 **Graph-Based Attention Models**: Recent work explores graph-based transformer architectures that can better handle long-form content and feedback documents. These models use both intra-node and inter-node attention mechanisms to create richer relevance contexts while maintaining computational efficiency  [231648324 | Yu et al. | 2021 | Citations: 22]

 **Hierarchical Label Relationship Modeling**: Researchers are developing specialized architectures like the HG-transformer that convert text into graph structures and employ multi-attention mechanisms across word, sentence, and graph levels. These approaches incorporate weighted loss functions based on semantic label distances  [267320479 | Tarekegn et al. | 2024 | Citations: 8]  [222127391 | Gong et al. | 2020 | Citations: 57]

 **Advanced Feedback Integration**: There is significant activity in developing frameworks that combine multiple aspects of feedback processing. Current work includes integrating relevance matching with sentence-level semantic matching approaches  [270341565 | Pan et al. | 2024 | Citations: 2]  [212725119 | Wang et al. | 2020 | Citations: 13]

 **Full Document Interaction**: New approaches focus on avoiding information bottlenecks by modeling complete query-to-document interactions rather than breaking documents into chunks. This involves using attention operations within modular transformer frameworks to aggregate information from entire documents  [248571516 | Gao et al. | 2022 | Citations: 13]

 **Hierarchical Feature Processing**: Research is progressing on transformer-based frameworks that incorporate both feature calibration and deeply supervised aggregation. These systems aim to merge and preserve semantic and detail information across multiple levels while enabling multi-granularity supervision  [254129525 | Dai et al. | 2022 | Citations: 2]

 **Architecture Adaptation**: Work continues on developing flexible frameworks that can adapt to different transformer architectures or any architecture containing attention modules, allowing for greater versatility in implementation  [266738521 | Wu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 2]

citations.title: [231648324 | Yu et al. | 2021 | Citations: 22]
snippets: Most research on pseudo relevance feedback (PRF) has been done in vector space and probabilistic retrieval models. This paper shows that Transformer-based rerankers can also benefit from the extra context that PRF provides. It presents PGT, a graph-based Transformer that sparsifies attention between graph nodes to enable PRF while avoiding the high computational complexity of most Transformer architectures. Experiments show that PGT improves upon non-PRF Transformer reranker, and it is at least as accurate as Transformer PRF models that use full attention, but with lower computational costs.

citations.title: [248571516 | Gao et al. | 2022 | Citations: 13]
snippets: Long document re-ranking has been a challenging problem for neural re-rankers based on deep language models like BERT. Early work breaks the documents into short passage-like chunks. These chunks are independently mapped to scalar scores or latent vectors, which are then pooled into a final relevance score. These encode-and-pool methods however inevitably introduce an information bottleneck: the low dimension representations. In this paper, we propose instead to model full query-to-document interaction, leveraging the attention operation and modular Transformer re-ranker framework. First, document chunks are encoded independently with an encoder module. An interaction module then encodes the query and performs joint attention from the query to all document chunk representations. We demonstrate that the model can use this new degree of freedom to aggregate important information from the entire document.

question: Can LLMs learn new information when trained on supervised fine-tuning (SFT)?

sections.title: Introduction to SFT
sections.text:
TLDR; Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is a critical training process that adapts pre-trained LLMs to specific tasks by teaching them from labeled input-output pairs. It addresses the fundamental mismatch between LLMs' basic completion-focused pre-training and the need for more controlled, task-oriented responses. (6 sources)

Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) serves as a crucial second-stage training process that builds upon the foundation laid during pre-training  [60030950 | Miltenburg et al. | 2018 | Citations: 2]. Unlike the unsupervised nature of pre-training, which focuses on completing any text pattern, SFT specifically aims to enhance LLMs' ability to follow human instructions and produce more relevant, targeted responses  [259244145 | Yue et al. | 2023 | Citations: 2].

The technical implementation of SFT involves adjusting a pre-trained LLM's model weights based on discrepancies between predicted and desired outputs  [271855813 | Zhang et al. | 2024 | Citations: 0]  [275470566 | Hogan et al. | 2025 | Citations: 1]. This process typically utilizes carefully curated datasets containing labeled examples that demonstrate the intended behaviors and outcomes for specific tasks  [270440880 | Wu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 5].

A notable aspect of SFT is its effectiveness in maintaining a balance - the models retain their broad knowledge base while gaining specialization in targeted areas  [270440880 | Wu et al. | 2024 | Citations: 5]. This capability has been extensively validated through research, including pioneering work that demonstrated how SFT combined with reinforcement learning could effectively align language models with human intent  (Wu et al._1,  2024)  [246426909 | Ouyang et al. | 2022 | Citations: 11999].

citations.title: [259244145 | Yue et al. | 2023 | Citations: 2]
snippets: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) aims to enhance the capacity of large language models (LLMs) to follow human instructions better (Ouyang et al., 2022).

citations.title: [246426909 | Ouyang et al. | 2022 | Citations: 11999]
snippets: Making language models bigger does not inherently make them better at following a user's intent. For example, large language models can generate outputs that are untruthful, toxic, or simply not helpful to the user. In other words, these models are not aligned with their users. In this paper, we show an avenue for aligning language models with user intent on a wide range of tasks by fine-tuning with human feedback. Starting with a set of labeler-written prompts and prompts submitted through the OpenAI API, we collect a dataset of labeler demonstrations of the desired model behavior, which we use to fine-tune GPT-3 using supervised learning. We then collect a dataset of rankings of model outputs, which we use to further fine-tune this supervised model using reinforcement learning from human feedback. We call the resulting models InstructGPT. In human evaluations on our prompt distribution, outputs from the 1.3B parameter InstructGPT model are preferred to outputs from the 175B GPT-3, despite having 100x fewer parameters. Moreover, InstructGPT models show improvements in truthfulness and reductions in toxic output generation while having minimal performance regressions on public NLP datasets. Even though InstructGPT still makes simple mistakes, our results show that fine-tuning with human feedback is a promising direction for aligning language models with human intent.

Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides the model with labeled examples of desired input-output pairs specific to the task.

citations.title: [60030950 | Miltenburg et al. | 2018 | Citations: 2]
snippets: The first stage, known as pre-training, is an unsupervised process in which models are trained on vast amounts of unlabelled textual data containing billions or even trillions of tokens from diverse sources such as web pages, books, and encyclopaedias. This stage allows LLMs to acquire and encode general linguistic and world knowledge. The second stage, known as Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), involves further training the model on labelled datasets containing explicit instruction-output pairs. SFT aims to enhance the model's ability to understand and follow human-provided instructions, ensuring its responses are more relevant, specific, and aligned with user expectations.

sections.title: Knowledge Acquisition Capabilities
sections.text:
TLDR; Research shows that LLMs primarily rely on their pre-trained knowledge rather than actually acquiring new facts during SFT. When new knowledge must be learned through SFT, it happens slowly and increases the risk of hallucination. (4 sources)

While SFT is designed to adapt LLMs to specific tasks, its effectiveness in actual knowledge acquisition presents some important limitations. Recent research has revealed that LLMs tend to heavily depend on their pre-existing pre-trained knowledge rather than truly incorporating new information during the fine-tuning process  [271892126 | Li et al. | 2024 | Citations: 2].

When attempting to teach LLMs new factual information through SFT, empirical evidence indicates significant challenges. Studies have found that when models encounter new knowledge during fine-tuning, they learn this information considerably slower compared to concepts that align with their existing knowledge base. More concerning is that once these new knowledge points are eventually learned, they appear to linearly increase the model's tendency toward hallucination  [269635770 | Gekhman et al. | 2024 | Citations: 104].

However, there are nuanced conditions under which knowledge acquisition through SFT might be possible. Research suggests that fine-tuning on partially mastered knowledge - particularly in scenarios where the model has a reasonable chance of producing correct outputs under non-greedy decoding - may facilitate genuine knowledge integration while helping reduce hallucination risks  (Li et al._1,  2024).

These findings support the broader understanding that while SFT excels at teaching LLMs how to utilize their existing knowledge more effectively, its primary role appears to be in behavioral adaptation and efficient knowledge application rather than true knowledge expansion <Model name="Anthropic" version="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022">.

citations.title: [269635770 | Gekhman et al. | 2024 | Citations: 104]
snippets: When large language models are aligned via supervised fine-tuning, they may encounter new factual information that was not acquired through pre-training...We demonstrate that large language models struggle to acquire new factual knowledge through fine-tuning, as fine-tuning examples that introduce new knowledge are learned significantly slower than those consistent with the model's knowledge. However, we also find that as the examples with new knowledge are eventually learned, they linearly increase the model's tendency to hallucinate...our results highlight the risk in introducing new factual knowledge through fine-tuning, and support the view that large language models mostly acquire factual knowledge through pre-training, whereas fine-tuning teaches them to use it more efficiently.

sections.title: Data Requirements and Limitations
sections.text:
TLDR; Recent research shows that surprisingly small datasets (as few as 60-1,000 examples) can effectively fine-tune LLMs for specific tasks. However, SFT faces diminishing returns with larger datasets and may actually harm already-capable models, highlighting the importance of data quality over quantity. (5 sources)

Studies have demonstrated that SFT can be remarkably efficient in terms of data requirements. Recent experimental findings indicate that as few as 60 data points during the SFT stage can successfully activate pre-encoded knowledge in LLMs and enable them to perform specific tasks like question-answering  [272832639 | Ye et al. | 2024 | Citations: 2]. Similarly, successful implementations have been achieved with very modest datasets, such as a compilation of just 1,000 examples  (Wu et al._2,  2024).

However, this efficiency comes with important caveats regarding scalability and optimal performance. Research has identified diminishing returns as SFT dataset size and quality increase, particularly noticeable when working with stronger base models that already possess extensive domain knowledge  [275954349 | Wang et al. | 2025 | Citations: 13]. In some cases, applying SFT to highly capable base models can potentially degrade their performance if proper quality controls aren't maintained  [275954349 | Wang et al. | 2025 | Citations: 13].

To optimize SFT outcomes, attention must be paid to two key factors: data quality and diversity. High-quality, well-curated datasets consistently demonstrate superior results compared to larger but lower-quality collections  (Wu et al._2,  2024). Additionally, when implementing SFT with incomplete or imperfect datasets, models may experience difficulties in establishing accurate mappings between inputs and desired outputs, particularly evident in reasoning-intensive tasks like question-answering  [266725491 | Li et al. | 2023 | Citations: 2]. This challenge emphasizes the importance of thoughtful dataset curation over pursuing sheer volume in SFT applications.

snippets: However, LLMs trained with SFT sometimes make simple mistakes and result in hallucinations on reasoning tasks such as question-answering. Without external feedback, it is difficult for SFT to learn a good mapping between the question and the desired answer, especially with a small dataset.

snippets: Our experiments, involving four LLMs from three different model families, focus on three key factors: the amount of data required for SFT, the impact of different SFT datasets on model performance, and how data requirements vary across LLMs. The results show that as few as 60 data points during the SFT stage can activate the knowledge encoded during pre-training, enabling LLMs to perform the QA task.

citations.title: [275954349 | Wang et al. | 2025 | Citations: 13]
snippets: While these approaches have shown significant gains on weaker base models such as Mistral (Jiang et al., 2023) or LLaMA3 (Dubey et al., 2024), diminishing returns become evident as SFT dataset size and quality scale up. This limitation is particularly pronounced for already-powerful base models (non-SFTed), such as Qwen2.5-base (Yang et al., 2024a), Qwen2.5-Math-base (Yang et al., 2024b), or DeepSeek-Coder-V2-base (Guo et al., 2024), which have undergone extensive domain-adaptive pretraining on reasoning-focused corpora comprising hundreds of billions of tokens. Our experiments in section 3 reveal that applying SFT to these models can even degrade performance without stringent quality control.

sections.title: Types of New Knowledge Acquired
sections.text:
TLDR; SFT enables LLMs to acquire new capabilities in three main ways: improved task-specific performance, enhanced instruction comprehension, and better handling of novel situations. The effectiveness varies based on how closely the new knowledge aligns with the model's existing capabilities. (8 sources)

* **Task-Specific Performance Enhancement**: SFT proves highly effective at improving performance in specialized domains including instruction following, sentiment analysis, medical report generation, and code generation  (Wang et al._1,  2025). This enhancement occurs because SFT injects new knowledge or activates existing capabilities related to these specific tasks, as evidenced by changes in the model's parameters  [265158175 | Ni et al. | 2023 | Citations: 7].

* **Multilingual Understanding**: When fine-tuned with limited instruction pairs (even as few as 0-5,000 examples), LLMs can begin comprehending new languages, though this may initially manifest as code-switching behavior until sufficient mastery is achieved  [264591406 | Zhao et al. | 2023 | Citations: 5].

* **Domain Adaptation**: Models can be taught to handle completely new domains of knowledge, as demonstrated by successful sports event coverage training  [268819437 | Mecklenburg et al. | 2024 | Citations: 23]. This includes developing specialized response patterns for specific demographics and viewpoints  [270711081 | Chuang et al. | 2024 | Citations: 12].

* **Unseen Task Generalization**: Through careful instruction tuning, models can develop the ability to apply learned principles to previously unseen tasks  [265067168 | Huang et al. | 2023 | Citations: 731]  [255096269 | Iyer et al. | 2022 | Citations: 261]. This generalization capability extends beyond mere memorization of training examples to encompass broader problem-solving abilities.

* **Efficient Knowledge Utilization**: Perhaps most notably, SFT doesn't necessarily add new knowledge to the model but rather teaches the model to access and utilize its existing knowledge more effectively  [264591406 | Zhao et al. | 2023 | Citations: 5]  [269449935 | Bai et al. | 2024 | Citations: 139]. This distinction is crucial for understanding the true scope of what SFT accomplishes versus what it cannot.

snippets: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) aims to further enhance the capability of LLMs to follow instructions...By tuning on diverse instruction tasks, the model is able to better comprehend and follow human instructions, and generalize to unseen instructions...We find that when fine-tuning with a small amount of instruction pairs (between 0 to 5,000) on languages that LLaMA is not familiar with (such as Chinese), the responses exhibit code-switching behavior.

citations.title: [265067168 | Huang et al. | 2023 | Citations: 731]
snippets: While LLMs acquire substantial knowledge and capabilities during the pre-training stage, it's crucial to recognize that pretraining primarily optimizes for completion. Consequently, pre-trained LLMs fundamentally served as completion machines, which can lead to a misalignment between the next-word prediction objective of LLMs and the user's objective of obtaining desired responses. To bridge this gap, SFT (Zhang et al., 2023d) has been introduced, which involves further training LLMs using a meticulously annotated set of (instruction, response) pairs, resulting in enhanced capabilities and improved controllability of LLMs. Furthermore, recent studies (Chung et al., 2022;(Iyer et al., 2022) have confirmed the effectiveness of supervised fine-tuning to achieve exceptional performance on unseen tasks, showcasing their remarkable generalization abilities.

citations.title: [255096269 | Iyer et al. | 2022 | Citations: 261]
snippets: Recent work has shown that fine-tuning large pre-trained language models on a collection of tasks described via instructions, a.k.a. instruction-tuning, improves their zero and few-shot generalization to unseen tasks. However, there is a limited understanding of the performance trade-offs of different decisions made during the instruction-tuning process. These decisions include the scale and diversity of the instruction-tuning benchmark, different task sampling strategies, fine-tuning with and without demonstrations, training using specialized datasets for reasoning and dialogue, and finally, the fine-tuning objectives themselves. In this paper, we characterize the effect of instruction-tuning decisions on downstream task performance when scaling both model and benchmark sizes. To this end, we create OPT-IML Bench: a large benchmark for Instruction Meta-Learning (IML) of 2000 NLP tasks consolidated into task categories from 8 existing benchmarks, and prepare an evaluation framework to measure three types of model generalizations: to tasks from fully held-out categories, to held-out tasks from seen categories, and to held-out instances from seen tasks. Through the lens of this framework, we first present insights about instruction-tuning decisions as applied to OPT-30B and further exploit these insights to train OPT-IML 30B and 175B, which are instruction-tuned versions of OPT. OPT-IML demonstrates all three generalization abilities at both scales on four different evaluation benchmarks with diverse tasks and input formats -- PromptSource, FLAN, Super-NaturalInstructions, and UnifiedSKG. Not only does it significantly outperform OPT on all benchmarks but is also highly competitive with existing models fine-tuned on each specific benchmark. We release OPT-IML at both scales, together with the OPT-IML Bench evaluation framework.
